editorial:
Imagine living a double life where you are a respected city leader by day and a daring thief by night. That is exactly what you get with this story about Deacon Brodie. He is a talented cabinet maker who everyone in town looks up to, but he has a secret wild side. He loves money, luxury, and the thrill of stealing from the rich. The movie captures that old-school Edinburgh vibe perfectly, making you feel like you are walking through those foggy streets while Brodie pulls off his latest scam. It is a fun ride that shows how greed can make someone feel invincible.

The acting is solid and keeps you interested even when the plot slows down. You will love seeing how Brodie balances his high-society life with his criminal habits, though some parts of the movie feel a bit slow. If you enjoy true crime stories from the past, you should definitely give this a try. To get the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or searching for a digital copy to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look at the costumes and sets. Adding a physical Blu-ray to your collection is also a great move if you love historical dramas.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Brodie tries to rob the Customs and Excise office. He gets caught red-handed, and his secret life is exposed to everyone. After a huge trial that the whole city talks about, he is sentenced to death. In a cruel twist of irony, he ends up being hanged on the very same gallows that he helped design. It is a sad but fair ending that shows his pride was his downfall.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and historical stories.
